_what_this_is: The goals the loop is working TOWARD, each with a machine-readable done-condition. ⛔ THIS IS NOT THE LEDGER. The ledger holds ITEMS — units of work a cycle can take; this holds OBJECTIVES, which no single cycle completes and which outlive the cycle that advances them. An item is done when its work is done; a goal is done when a condition computed from committed artifacts says so.
_why_this_exists:
⛔⛔ THE ONE REAL GOAL IN PLAY WAS PROSE IN A DIFFERENT FILE'S SCOPE NOTE, AND NOTHING READ IT. trimcrae set 'get ASO v2 submission ready' on 2026-08-30 and it lived inside `autonomy-state.json`'s `budget_hold.authorised_exceptions` — a field about SPENDING — where it authorised a budget exception and tracked nothing. Meanwhile `publish_bar` computes seven clauses from committed artifacts, `health.py` grades twelve conditions and `continuity.py` refuses to go quiet while ready work exists. The goal that justified spending against a budget hold was the least instrumented object in the system.
⚠ MEASURED 2026-09-01 (CYC-0090), and it is why this file exists rather than being a good idea: a full session of real work — a published Zenodo archive, two hardening rounds, four process defects found and fixed — moved `publish_bar` from 4/7 to 4/7. Every individual step was warranted. Nothing measured the distance to the objective, so nothing could say the distance had not closed. trimcrae asked for it directly: 'For now, the loop should just track the goal of the ASO paper.'
_how_to_read_it: `python3 research/autonomy/goal_progress.py --check`. It computes each goal's done-condition live and prints the distance. ⛔ IT NEVER READS A STORED VERDICT: `readings` below is a HISTORY for spotting a goal that is not moving, and a reader who trusts it instead of recomputing has the staleness problem this file was built to end (CLAUDE.md §4 — a populated field is not a measured one).
_scope_2026_09_01: ⭐ ONE GOAL, DELIBERATELY. trimcrae: 'For now, the loop should just track the goal of the ASO paper.' The schema admits more; adding one is a decision, not a formality, because a goals file that accumulates aspirations is a wish list and this repository already has a ledger for work.

goals.title: PUB-ASO's journal submission package is complete and stays current
goals.set_by: trimcrae, 2026-09-04, choosing between three successors offered after GOAL-ASO-V2 was measured met: the journal submission package — the loop assembles everything the venue asks for and stops there; submitting stays his.
goals._set_by_note: ⛔ RECORDED AS A CHOICE FROM A NAMED SET, NOT AS A PARAPHRASE OF A FREE SENTENCE. The other two options were 'fix the archive first' (the deposit drift in preprint checklist §3-vii) and 'go back to the wider portfolio'. He picked the package, so the archive gap stays an open item rather than the objective, and the portfolio scope stays narrowed.

done_condition.requires: every clause passes on the commit being submitted
done_condition._reads: n_passed == n_clauses. ⛔ THE CLAUSE COUNT IS READ FROM THE TOOL, NEVER TYPED. ⚠ AND `may_post` IS EXPECTED TO BE FALSE HERE FOREVER: `authority_permits` refuses venue 'journal' by design — 'journal submission always escalates (D4); no bar reaches it' — so the clauses are the goal and the authority is his signature, not a gate to clear.

goals._what_done_does_not_mean: ⛔ IT DOES NOT MEAN SUBMITTED, AND IT DOES NOT PICK THE JOURNAL. Which venue this goes to is his call (D4) and the package as assembled targets *Nucleic Acid Therapeutics* — that is who the cover letter is addressed to and whose limits the packet grades against. A different venue means a re-addressed letter and a re-graded packet, which is work, not a formality.
goals._blocks_on_a_human_note: 2026-09-04 journal preparation is complete; see codex-handover.json aso_submission for the frozen manual NAT package, independent focused review, artifact checks and full release verification. Remaining actions are the author final approval, current submission declarations and submission itself. Historical publish_bar readings below refer to the canonical manuscript and are preserved; no automated publish_bar result is claimed for the separate condensed journal package.

readings._note:
⭐ THE TRACKER READS MET ON DAY ONE, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT STATE FOR THIS GOAL RATHER THAN A SIGN IT IS EMPTY. `goal_progress.py --check` computes 8/8 at round 34's reviewed pin 3d5c709b69bc — the same basis it used for GOAL-ASO-V2, because the clauses bind to a reviewed commit and HEAD is never one. This goal is a MAINTENANCE goal: 'complete and stays current' is satisfied now and goes OPEN the moment a clause fails, a packet file stops existing, or a round returns a blocker. A tracker that only ever reads OPEN would be measuring a build; this one measures a standing state.
⚠ THE OTHER READING, TAKEN THE SAME MINUTE AND ON A DIFFERENT BASIS, SO NOBODY READS THEM AS ONE: at HEAD (the v2-record merge commit) with `--venue journal` the bar is 7 of 8, open on `preflight_full_green` alone — no PREFLIGHT_FULL receipt exists for that commit. The manuscript is byte-identical between HEAD and the pin, so the difference is entirely the receipt's binding. ⛔ That clause is the loop's remaining work on this goal and it is deliberately NOT run yet: the receipt binds to a commit, and running it against a HEAD that will move spends 25 minutes to learn nothing about the commit actually submitted.

goals._why_pub_aso_is_not_in_his_ready_to_post: ⛔ DELIBERATE, AND IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Setting `next_act: journal_submission` on PUB-ASO would put a row in `ready-to-post.json`, and `ready_to_post.py` grades that row against HEAD — where the bar reads one clause short because no PREFLIGHT_FULL receipt exists for HEAD. He would get a queue entry reading NOT-READY for a paper whose blocking clause is a receipt binding, which is worse than no entry. ★ The row goes in when the submission commit is pinned and its receipt is recorded — at which point the row reads READY and means it.
